incident: IcedID to XingLocker ransomware in 24 hours

sources.title: IcedID to XingLocker Ransomware in 24 Hours - The DFIR Report (2021-10-18)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (phishing IcedID via regsvr32), hops (beachhead->DC remote service running spoolsv.exe, jump psexec_psh to other hosts, CS to critical server), cred access (LSASS cached creds, PtH named pipe, admin creds in 4 min), impact (XingLocker/Mountlocker via wmic+batch on DC/external server/multiple servers), ~23h

narrative_before: In a late-July 2021 intrusion the DFIR Report observed IcedID delivered by phishing and executed on the beachhead with regsvr32.exe, dropping ikaqkk.dll (rundll32) and loading Cobalt Strike beacons (DLLHost.exe via process hollowing; kaslose.dll via curl+regsvr32; an HTA/PowerShell in-memory beacon). Within four minutes of beacon activity the actors read cached credentials from LSASS and 'gained administrative credentials' (a Mimikatz-style pass-the-hash named pipe was seen). About two hours in, IcedID pulled the next-stage beacon; around three hours in beacons were deployed broadly. Lateral movement to a domain controller created a remote service running spoolsv.exe (Cobalt Strike), and jump psexec_psh moved beacons to other hosts including a 'critical' server (kaslose64.dll). kasper.bat (1,698 lines) killed processes and disabled security tools on a file server, and an 'important' host had backup utilities disabled. XingLocker (a Mountlocker variant) was deployed via wmic and batch scripts (start.bat -> rundll32 update64.dll,start), first observed on the DC and an external server, around 23 hours after intrusion; RecoveryManual.html was dropped.

detection_moments.description: IcedID executed via regsvr32 on the beachhead; Cobalt Strike beacons loaded; within 4 minutes LSASS cached creds read and admin credentials obtained.
detection_moments.evidence: 'A phishing campaign delivered IcedID, which was executed on the beachhead with regsvr32.exe ... Within four minutes they gained administrative credentials' - IcedID to XingLocker, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: ~3h: lateral movement to DC via remote service (spoolsv.exe), jump psexec_psh to other hosts, second beacon on a critical server.
detection_moments.evidence: 'lateral movement from the beachhead, which created a remote service running spoolsv.exe ... Cobalt Strike jump psexec_psh ... A second kaslose64.dll Beacon was executed right after the initial lateral movement' - IcedID to XingLocker

detection_moments.description: ~23h: XingLocker deployed via wmic/batch, first observed on the DC and an external server; security tools/backup utilities disabled beforehand.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Ransomware deployment: Via wmic and batch scripts ... The domain controller (first observed), an external server, and multiple servers' - IcedID to XingLocker

attack_path: phishing IcedID executed via regsvr32; Cobalt Strike loaded (T1566/T1218.010)
remote service creation running spoolsv.exe (Cobalt Strike) on the domain controller (T1021.002/T1569.002)
jump psexec_psh delivering kaslose64.dll beacon to a critical server (T1021.002)
XingLocker executed via wmic and batch scripts on servers (T1047/T1486)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role / importance only; victim sector not stated.
No exfiltration observed (may have used the encrypted Cobalt Strike channel).
Report does not confirm domain admin specifically ('administrative credentials'); 'important' host not confirmed to be a dedicated backup server.
Moments are the report's activity markers (IcedID+creds, lateral, encryption), not a defender detection timeline.
